content: AI is a field of computer science focused on systems that perform tasks associated with human intelligence.
Machine learning allows computers to learn patterns from data rather than being explicitly programmed for every case.
Supervised learning uses labeled examples to learn a mapping between inputs and target outputs.
Unsupervised learning discovers patterns or structures in data without predefined labels.
Deep learning uses neural networks with multiple layers to learn complex representations.
Natural Language Processing enables computers to process and understand human language.
A Large Language Model is trained on large collections of text and can perform many language-related tasks.
Generative AI creates new content such as text, images, audio, video, and code from user instructions.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation retrieves external information and provides it as context to a language model.
A basic RAG pipeline includes loading, splitting, embedding, vector storage, retrieval, prompting, and generation.
A document loader reads information from sources such as TXT, PDF, CSV, websites, or databases.
Chunking divides large documents into smaller pieces so relevant information can be retrieved efficiently.
Chunk overlap preserves some shared text between neighboring chunks and can help maintain context.
An embedding converts text or other information into a numerical vector representing semantic characteristics.
Cosine similarity measures the angle-based similarity between vectors and is commonly used in semantic search.
A vector database stores embeddings and supports efficient similarity search.
FAISS is a library for efficient similarity search and clustering of dense vectors.
Chroma is a vector database commonly used for AI and RAG prototypes and applications.
Pinecone is a managed vector database designed for similarity search and AI applications.
Weaviate is a vector database that supports semantic search and AI-oriented retrieval workflows.
A retriever finds documents or chunks that are relevant to a user's query.
Hybrid search combines different retrieval approaches, such as keyword matching and semantic vector search.
Reranking evaluates initially retrieved results and reorders them according to their relevance.
Metadata provides additional information such as source, date, category, author, or document identifier.
An AI hallucination is an unsupported or incorrect generated claim presented as if it were factual.
Grounding means generating an answer using reliable information supplied by external sources or retrieved context.
A prompt is an instruction or input provided to an AI model to guide its response.
Retrieved documents can be inserted into a prompt so the model can use external knowledge when answering.
PDFs can contain reports, manuals, research papers, and policies that can be loaded and indexed for retrieval.
CSV rows can be transformed into searchable documents while preserving useful columns as metadata.
TXT files are simple sources for RAG experiments because their contents can be loaded directly and split into chunks.
RAG evaluation measures retrieval quality and the correctness, relevance, completeness, and grounding of generated answers.
Query rewriting transforms a user's question into a retrieval-friendly query to improve search results.
Multi-query retrieval creates multiple variations of a question and searches using each variation.
Contextual compression reduces retrieved material to the portions most relevant to the user's question.
Agentic RAG allows an AI agent to decide when and how to retrieve information using tools or knowledge sources.
Access control ensures users retrieve only documents and information they are authorized to access.
RAG systems should protect sensitive documents, prompts, retrieved context, and generated responses.
A knowledge base is a collection of information that an AI application can search to answer user questions.
Semantic search retrieves information based on meaning rather than requiring exact keyword matches.
